description: PRD-102: Coordinator Architecture — Full research + design PRD. Study blackboard architecture, HTN planning, BDI agents. Design the CoordinatorService that decomposes missions into tasks, assigns agents, monitors progress, and handles failures.

userStories.title: Research coordination architectures
userStories.description: As a researcher, I need to study how existing systems coordinate multi-agent workflows so that our coordinator design is grounded in proven patterns
acceptanceCriteria: Study Blackboard Architecture (Nii 1986, Hayes-Roth) — shared workspace, knowledge sources, control component
Study HTN (Hierarchical Task Network) planning — task decomposition, method selection, preconditions
Study BDI (Belief-Desire-Intention) agents — how agents form plans from goals
Study Symphony's WORKFLOW.md pattern — policy-as-code, reconciliation loop
Study CrewAI's crew orchestration — sequential/hierarchical/consensual processes
Study AutoGen's group chat manager — speaker selection, termination conditions
Study LangGraph's state machine approach — nodes, edges, conditional routing
Comparison table: pattern, strengths, weaknesses, fit for Automatos
Write to PRD section: '## 2. Prior Art: Coordination Architectures'
userStories.notes: Use DeepWiki for CrewAI (crewAIInc/crewAI), AutoGen (microsoft/autogen), LangGraph (langchain-ai/langgraph). For Blackboard/HTN/BDI, use web search for academic summaries. Focus on what we can ADOPT, not just catalog.

userStories.title: Research LLM planning capabilities
userStories.description: As a researcher, I need to understand how well current LLMs decompose complex goals so that our coordinator prompt design is realistic
acceptanceCriteria: Research LLM task decomposition accuracy — what models can reliably break down goals
Study prompt patterns for planning: chain-of-thought, tree-of-thought, ReAct, plan-and-solve
Research how Symphony uses WORKFLOW.md to constrain LLM planning
Document model tier recommendations: which models for planning vs execution
Address: what happens when the plan is wrong — replanning triggers and strategies
Write to PRD section: '## 3. LLM Planning Capabilities & Constraints'
Include example coordinator prompts for task decomposition
Include failure mode analysis — how bad plans manifest and how to detect them
userStories.notes: PRD-100 Open Question #2: 'How much planning capability do current LLMs actually have for task decomposition?' This story answers that question. Test with real examples from the platform — e.g., 'Research EU AI Act compliance' from PRD-100's example flow.

userStories.title: Design coordinator service architecture
userStories.description: As a platform architect, I need the CoordinatorService designed with clear responsibilities, interfaces, and integration points
acceptanceCriteria: Define CoordinatorService class with all public methods and their signatures
Methods: create_mission(goal, config) → run_id, plan_mission(run_id) → task_graph, execute_mission(run_id), monitor_mission(run_id) → status, cancel_mission(run_id)
Define coordinator lifecycle: receive goal → decompose → create tasks → assign agents → monitor → verify → human review
Define how coordinator uses ContextService — new COORDINATOR context mode with specific sections
Define how coordinator calls AgentFactory.execute_with_prompt for each task
Define inter-task data flow — how Task 2 gets Task 1's output
Write to PRD section: '## 4. CoordinatorService Architecture'
Include sequence diagram (mermaid or ASCII) for full mission lifecycle
Include module placement: where CoordinatorService lives in the codebase hierarchy
userStories.notes: The coordinator is NOT an agent — it's a service that uses agents. It lives at orchestrator/services/ alongside heartbeat_service.py. It creates orchestration_runs (PRD-101 schema) and dispatches to AgentFactory. Read heartbeat_service.py for the closest existing pattern — orchestrator_tick_llm already does simple multi-agent coordination.

userStories.title: Design agent assignment strategy
userStories.description: As a platform architect, I need agent assignment logic designed so that the coordinator picks the right agent for each task
acceptanceCriteria: Define assignment algorithm: task requirements → agent capabilities matching
Handle roster agent selection — match task_type to agent skills/tools
Handle contractor agent spawning — when no roster agent fits, define contractor config
Define model-per-role strategy — how coordinator selects models for different task types
Address load balancing — what if the best agent is already busy (heartbeat active)
Write to PRD section: '## 5. Agent Assignment Strategy'
Include decision tree (ASCII) for assignment logic
Connect to PRD-104 (Ephemeral Agents) — reference but don't duplicate
userStories.notes: The tool_router already matches tools to agents. Agent skills are stored in the skills table. The assignment algorithm should leverage existing data — agent.skill, agent.model, agent tool assignments. Don't build a recommendation engine — start with rule-based matching.

userStories.title: Design failure handling and replanning
userStories.description: As a platform architect, I need failure handling designed so that missions recover gracefully from task failures
acceptanceCriteria: Define failure taxonomy: task timeout, agent error, verification failure, budget exceeded, human rejection
Define retry strategy per failure type — retry same agent, retry different agent, retry different model, escalate to human
Define replanning triggers — when does the coordinator re-decompose the remaining work
Study Symphony's continuation vs retry distinction — adopt if applicable
Define circuit breaker — when to stop retrying and fail the mission
Write to PRD section: '## 6. Failure Handling & Recovery'
Include state transition diagram specifically for failure paths
Address: partial success — what if 3/5 tasks complete but 2 fail
userStories.notes: The existing task_reconciler.py already handles stall detection and auto-retry for simple tasks. Study its patterns. The coordinator failure handling builds on top of this but adds mission-level awareness — a single task failure might not fail the mission.

userStories.title: Design human review integration
userStories.description: As a platform architect, I need human review gates designed so that missions have appropriate oversight
acceptanceCriteria: Define review gate types: plan approval, task output review, mission completion review
Define UI flow — how human sees the plan, approves/modifies, reviews outputs
Define autonomy levels: full-approval (review everything), milestone-approval (review at key points), autonomous (review at end only)
Connect to existing board UI — mission tasks appear as board_tasks with project label
Define notification mechanism — how human is alerted when review is needed
Write to PRD section: '## 7. Human Review & Oversight'
Include wireframe sketches (ASCII) for key review screens
Address: what happens if human doesn't respond (timeout, escalation)
userStories.notes: The existing board already shows tasks. The report grading system (PRD-76) already has human review with star ratings. The mission review should integrate with both — show tasks on board, show reports for review, capture human feedback. Don't design new UI from scratch — extend what exists.

userStories.title: Write PRD-102 opening and synthesis
userStories.description: As a document author, I need to write the opening sections synthesizing all research into a coherent coordinator design
acceptanceCriteria: Create docs/PRDS/102-COORDINATOR-ARCHITECTURE.md
Header: version, type, status, priority, dependencies (PRD-100, PRD-101)
Section 1: Problem Statement — what coordination capability is missing, why heartbeat_service isn't enough
Synthesize US-001 through US-006 findings into coherent narrative
Include 'Design Decisions Made' table — decision, chosen approach, rationale, alternatives considered
Include 'What This PRD Delivers' and 'What This PRD Does NOT Cover'
userStories.notes: Written LAST to synthesize. Follow PRD-100 style.

userStories.title: Write PRD-102 conclusion and implementation guidance
userStories.description: As a document author, I need to close PRD-102 with risks, acceptance criteria, and implementation-ready artifacts
acceptanceCriteria: Write '## 8. Coordinator Prompt Templates' — actual prompt text for task decomposition and monitoring
Write '## 9. Risk Register' — coordinator-specific risks
Write '## 10. Implementation Acceptance Criteria' — testable criteria
Write '## 11. Appendix: CoordinatorService Interface' — full Python class stub with docstrings
Write '## 12. Appendix: Context Mode Configuration' — COORDINATOR mode config for ContextService
Final review pass — all cross-references valid, no gaps
PRD-102 complete and ready for peer review
userStories.notes: The coordinator prompt is the most critical artifact — it's what actually drives the LLM to decompose missions. Spend time on this. Study how ContextService builds prompts for existing modes and follow the same pattern.
